# Jane Andrews

## Overview

- **Age:** Sixteen years old (in Volume 1)  <sub>[v1 c33 P46](../source/v01-c33.md#nw-v01-c33-p0046)</sub>
- **Gender:** Female  <sub>[v2 c6 P10](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0010)</sub>
- **Origin:** Avonlea  <sub>[v3 c8 P18](../source/v03-c08.md#nw-v03-c08-p0018)</sub>
- **Role:** School teacher  <sub>[v1 c36 P24](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0024), [v2 c4 P0](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0000), [v3 c18 P3](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0003)</sub>
- **Nicknames:** Mrs. Inglis  <sub>[v4 c2 P10](../source/v04-c02.md#nw-v04-c02-p0010)</sub>

## Appearance

Jane is described as plain, steady, and pink-cheeked. On her wedding day, she was almost lost to sight amidst her diamonds, white satin, tulle, lace, roses, and orange blossoms.

_Sources: [v1 c32 P18](../source/v01-c32.md#nw-v01-c32-p0018), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006), [v3 c2 P4](../source/v03-c02.md#nw-v03-c02-p0004), [v3 c41 P9](../source/v03-c41.md#nw-v03-c41-p0009), [v4 c2 P10](../source/v04-c02.md#nw-v04-c02-p0010)_

## Personality

Jane is a composed, practical, sensible, and unflappable person who remains unbothered by nerves during examinations. She is conscientious, neat, and amiable, though she can be strict or cross in the classroom to maintain order. She lacks imaginative or poetical tendencies, viewing poems strictly as lines and verses, and is known for never saying anything that would hurt anyone's feelings.

_Sources: [v1 c31 P30](../source/v01-c31.md#nw-v01-c31-p0030), [v1 c32 P18](../source/v01-c32.md#nw-v01-c32-p0018), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006), [v2 c4 P2](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0002), [v2 c4 P8](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0008), [v2 c13 P65](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0065), [v2 c26 P59](../source/v02-c26.md#nw-v02-c26-p0059), [v3 c2 P4](../source/v03-c02.md#nw-v03-c02-p0004), [v3 c5 P17](../source/v03-c05.md#nw-v03-c05-p0017), [v4 c2 P10](../source/v04-c02.md#nw-v04-c02-p0010)_

## History

Jane grew up in Avonlea as part of the local youth cohort, participating in school activities and forming the Story Club with Anne Shirley, Diana Barry, and Ruby Gillis. While studying under Miss Stacy for the Queen's Entrance examination, she prepared for a teaching career and excelled in domestic science at Queen's Academy. Upon earning her teaching license, she was hired by the Newbridge school, where her disciplined methods earned her a place on the Inspector's Roll of Honor. She joined the Avonlea Village Improvement Society, serving on fundraising and morale committees with her peers. After later taking over the Avonlea school and eventually resigning, she traveled west to teach on the prairies. During a winter visit home, she reluctantly conveyed a marriage proposal to Anne on behalf of her shy brother Billy. She later returned to Avonlea and married Mr. Inglis, a Winnipeg millionaire, departing on a wedding tour to Europe before settling into a prosperous life in Winnipeg.

_Sources: [v1 c23 P41](../source/v01-c23.md#nw-v01-c23-p0041), [v1 c30 P15](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0015), [v1 c30 P21](../source/v01-c30.md#nw-v01-c30-p0021), [v1 c35 P6](../source/v01-c35.md#nw-v01-c35-p0006), [v1 c36 P24](../source/v01-c36.md#nw-v01-c36-p0024), [v2 c4 P2](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0002), [v2 c6 P10](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0010), [v2 c28 P3](../source/v02-c28.md#nw-v02-c28-p0003), [v3 c8 P12](../source/v03-c08.md#nw-v03-c08-p0012), [v3 c11 P0](../source/v03-c11.md#nw-v03-c11-p0000), [v3 c12 P10](../source/v03-c12.md#nw-v03-c12-p0010), [v3 c18 P3](../source/v03-c18.md#nw-v03-c18-p0003), [v3 c39 P18](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0018), [v3 c39 P27](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0027), [v3 c39 P35](../source/v03-c39.md#nw-v03-c39-p0035), [v4 c1 P20](../source/v04-c01.md#nw-v04-c01-p0020), [v4 c2 P10](../source/v04-c02.md#nw-v04-c02-p0010)_

## Quotes

> I guess we’ll get on all right. The main thing will be to keep order and a teacher has to be a little cross to do that. If my pupils won’t do as I tell them I shall punish them.  <sub>[v2 c4 P2](../source/v02-c04.md#nw-v02-c04-p0002)</sub>

> I wish there really were fairies. Wouldn’t it be nice to have three wishes granted you . . . or even only one? What would you wish for, girls, if you could have a wish granted? I’d wish to be rich and beautiful and clever.  <sub>[v2 c13 P32](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0032)</sub>

> I should rather call it a picture. A poem is lines and verses.  <sub>[v2 c13 P65](../source/v02-c13.md#nw-v02-c13-p0065)</sub>
